caption:
A hash is one-way: you can check a password against it, but you can't turn it back into the password.

Why slow? Fast hashes like MD5 or SHA-256 can be guessed billions of times per second on a GPU. bcrypt and Argon2 are designed to be slow and expensive to guess.

Why salted? A random value added per user means two people with the password "123456" get different hashes.

Never encrypt passwords (encryption can be reversed) and never write your own.

Source: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet.

altText:
Never store passwords.

Store a slow, salted hash (bcrypt or Argon2).

If your database leaks, attackers should get gibberish, not your users' passwords.
